source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew verse numbering align throughout Exodus 9–11.

key_decisions.decision: Retains the divine hand, the field qualification, and every livestock category, rendering the collective flock term as sheep and goats.
Keeps the explicit distinction and absolute promise within the stated livestock context.
Retains all without silently reducing it to many or adding the field qualification not repeated in this verse; a note identifies the narrative tension with later animals.
Supplies the contextual purpose of sending and preserves the heavy-heart state without naming a causing agent.
Keeps both men gathering soot and Moses specifically throwing it, without identifying the kiln as a particular industrial or ritual installation.
Preserves the progression from soot to dust to bodily lesions and both affected groups without a modern disease diagnosis.
Retains the specialists’ bodily incapacity alongside the wider suffering without recasting it as merely loss of status.
Keeps the LORD explicitly as the hardening agent in this fulfillment and clarifies the hearers while retaining the prior-prediction formula.
Retains the heart image, all three recipients, and the stated knowing purpose rather than treating the heart as an anatomical target only.
Renders the unrealized possibility in context, not a claim that Pharaoh has already been exterminated.
Retains the standing image and both purposes, with the spare/establish range noted rather than replacing the statement with a later quotation.
Renders the self-exalting obstruction in natural English while preserving Pharaoh’s continued opposition as his own action.
Preserves the protective warning, all possessions, and explicit death of exposed people and animals without muting the harm.
Distinguishes Pharaoh’s court servants from the people under their control, retaining both fear and protective action.
Keeps the heart idiom, the contrasting failure to act, and the exposure of dependent people and animals.
Keeps Moses’ gesture distinct from the LORD’s action and retains fire as the ancient storm image rather than replacing all occurrences with lightning.
Preserves interwoven hail and fire and the repeated national-history comparison.
Retains comprehensive field destruction across human, animal, plant, and tree categories without extending the scope to those sheltered indoors.
Preserves Pharaoh’s confession, its this-time qualification, and the righteous/wrong contrast as his own words.
Retains the possible divine genitive in thunder, the appeal, and the renewed release promise rather than explaining his sincerity.
Keeps the promised location and prayer gesture, both weather changes, and the wider ownership claim.
Retains Moses’ explicit assessment and not-yet qualification without expanding it into a doctrine of repentance.
Retains the explicit crop exceptions and later growth, using the conventional spelt identification with uncertainty noted.
Preserves Pharaoh’s renewed sin and the servants’ participation, rendering the Hebrew singular heart with the shared subject in natural English.
Keeps the uncaused grammatical state and the mediated-word formula, distinct from the named agents in the preceding verse.
